text.arabic_uthmani: قَالَ ٱللَّهُ إِنِّى مُنَزِّلُهَا عَلَيْكُمْ ۖ فَمَن يَكْفُرْ بَعْدُ مِنكُمْ فَإِنِّىٓ أُعَذِّبُهُۥ عَذَابًۭا لَّآ أُعَذِّبُهُۥٓ أَحَدًۭا مِّنَ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ

words.gloss_range: direct authoritative saying that opens a completed divine answer and governs the quotation that follows
words.root_gloss_range: saying, speaking, declaring, and opinion; the local speaker and quote frame select authoritative declaration rather than casual report
words.prose: {{ar:قَالَ}} ({{tr:qāla}}) does not merely report that speech occurred. As a perfect speech verb with the named divine subject after it, it opens the answer as an issued declaration and makes the whole remaining ayah its quoted object. The word also resets the table scene from human petition to divine response, joining the Surah 5 divine-speech turns at 5:12, 5:110, 5:115, and the next turn at 5:116.

topics.headline: completed divine quote frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the promise, condition, and punishment as one directly attributed divine speech unit, not as loose narration.
topics.reason: The verb is perfect 3ms, its subject is the next word, and attachment evidence makes the rest of the ayah the quoted complement.

topics.headline: petition answered by declaration
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the scene change: the request of 5:114 has become an operative divine answer in 5:115.
topics.reason: Boundary rows tie 5:114 to 5:115, and the perfect reporting verb introduces the answer as already issued.

topics.headline: major divine speech-turn formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears this opening as part of the surah's formal dialogue sequence, with concrete links to 5:12, 5:110, and 5:116.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL inter-ayah rows give concrete Surah 5 speech-turn references, and no local syntax blocks the formulaic comparison.

words.gloss_range: the proper divine name as explicit nominative subject of the speech verb
words.root_gloss_range: deity, worship, devotion, refuge, and related derivational fields; locally the proper name identifies the speaker rather than a class term
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:Allāhu}}) fills the subject slot after the speech verb, so the quoted promise and warning are anchored before the first-person speech begins. The proper name keeps the answer from being anonymous or merely indirect, and as the worshipped divine name it gives the statement devotion-and-refuge weight while still functioning locally as the subject. Its placement after the verb gives the speaker a focused arrival. The word also matters inside the surah's juridical deity discourse: the proper name here differs from broader deity-language elsewhere, including 5:73 and 5:116, and it places disbelief and punishment under the same named speaker who grants the table.

topics.headline: named subject anchors the quotation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader knows before the first-person clause begins that the whole answer is attributed to the named divine speaker.
topics.reason: The noun is the explicit nominative subject of the preceding speech verb.

topics.headline: proper name with worship-refuge resonance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader receives the answer as the utterance of the worshipped divine name, while the local syntax keeps the word functioning as a proper subject rather than a title explanation.
topics.reason: The derivational field is relevant as lexical pressure, but the local role is the proper noun subject, not a separate predicate about deity.

topics.headline: speech authority inside Surah 5 discourse
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the table answer as a juridical divine declaration inside Surah 5's wider speech, deity, disbelief, and punishment fields.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows supply concrete Surah 5 links, including 5:73, 5:115, and 5:116, while the local word supplies the named speaker.

words.gloss_range: emphatic first-person opening of the promise clause
words.prose: {{ar:إِنِّى}} ({{tr:innī}}) opens the first quoted commitment with emphasis and first-person divine self-reference. It governs a nominal clause, so the sending-down is stabilized as a predication about the speaker. Its force is also local and paired: the first emphatic self-reference promises the table, while the later emphatic first-person consequence frame introduces the punishment consequence.

topics.headline: emphatic nominal promise
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the table's descent as a solemn divine commitment, not a neutral future note.
topics.reason: The particle opens an emphatic nominal clause whose predicate is the following active participle.

topics.headline: speaker and emphasis fused
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that emphasis and divine first-person agency arrive together in one bound form.
topics.reason: The form combines the emphatic particle with the first-person suffix.

topics.headline: promise balanced by later warning
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees mercy and warning held in matching emphatic frames inside one speech.
topics.reason: The ayah repeats the emphatic first-person frame at word 12, with the second occurrence opening the consequence clause.

words.gloss_range: the one sending it down, with the attached feminine object referring to the requested table
words.root_gloss_range: descent, alighting, caused sending-down, revelation/provision register, lodging, rank, and other branches; the local Form II participle selects caused divine sending-down
words.prose: {{ar:مُنَزِّلُهَا}} ({{tr:munazziluhā}}) is the core promise word: the active participle serves as the predicate of the emphatic clause and governs the feminine suffix that points back to the table requested in 5:112-5:114. Form II makes the descent a caused, weighty divine sending-down rather than self-movement, and the root's descent register lets the food request sound like a divine delivery from above. The word also answers the earlier imperative of 5:114 by changing a human request into divine self-description. Because this promise stands immediately before the conditional turn, the descent itself becomes the premise of the warning that follows.

topics.headline: active participle with table suffix
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the promised object as the same table already requested, grammatically held by the feminine suffix.
topics.reason: The word is the predicate of the emphatic clause and its object suffix refers to the prior feminine table.

topics.headline: intensive caused descent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the answer intensifies the descent form, while local grammar keeps it to divine sending-down of the table rather than every branch of the root.
topics.reason: The canonical local form is Form II active participle; accepted Form IV comparison is useful for contrast but does not replace the local form.

topics.headline: table request enters descent register
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the requested food as a divine descent and provision event, not merely as food being supplied.
topics.reason: The root field supports descent and divine sending-down, while the local complement and following preposition direct it to the addressed recipients.

topics.headline: imperative request becomes divine assertion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the earlier request of 5:114 answered at the same root, but transformed into a stronger divine declaration.
topics.reason: Boundary and echo rows connect the root from 5:114 to the active participle in 5:115.

topics.headline: promise beat before accountability
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the descent promise is immediately the premise for the following warning.
topics.reason: The promise clause closes before the conditional protasis, and distributional rows mark the active participle choice as salient.

words.gloss_range: upon you, marking the addressed group as descent target and accountable recipients
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَيْكُمْ}} ({{tr:ʿalaykum}}) makes the descent land on the addressed group. The preposition gives the table a downward target, and the suffix makes that target the very group later narrowed by the from-among-you phrase. The word therefore turns recipienthood into accountability: what comes upon them can later be rejected from among them. It also carries the upon-language of 5:114 into the answer, shifting the prayer's spatial frame onto the addressed disciples.

topics.headline: descent lands on the addressees
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the table not as generic provision but as a gift directed upon this addressed group.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the second-person plural suffix as recipient of the sending-down.

topics.headline: recipient group becomes possible source
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same group moving from recipients of descent to possible source of rejection.
topics.reason: The pronoun in this word and the pronoun in word 10 refer to the same addressed group.

topics.headline: prior petition's upon-frame answered
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the prayer's upon-language carried into the answer, now redirected to the addressed disciples.
topics.reason: Boundary rows connect the prepositional frame from 5:114 into the answer in 5:115.

words.gloss_range: consequential connector that turns the promise into the condition
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) is the hinge from gift to test. It binds the sending-down promise directly to the conditional opening, so the warning follows because the gift has been promised. As the first of the two paired connectors, it begins the visible chain from promise to condition to consequence.

topics.headline: gift becomes condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the warning is attached to the gift, not added as a separate afterthought.
topics.reason: The connector opens the conditional protasis immediately after the promise clause.

topics.headline: first link in paired connector chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah's logic in two visible connector steps: condition opener and consequence opener.
topics.reason: The first connector fuses with the conditional particle, while the second connector opens the apodosis.

words.gloss_range: whoever, opening a rational indefinite conditional subject
words.prose: {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}) opens the warning as a live condition rather than naming a culprit. It governs the jussive verb that follows and leaves the person indefinite within the addressed group. The condition then tightens through act, time, and source: whoever, disbelieves, afterward, from among you.

topics.headline: open conditional culprit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the threat as an open conditional possibility for any relevant member, not as a report about a named person.
topics.reason: The particle is conditional and controls the jussive verb in the protasis.

topics.headline: whoever becomes specified step by step
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the warning narrow from open whoever to the specific post-table group context.
topics.reason: The conditional subject begins the protasis, and the following verb has no explicit object while later words specify timing and group.

words.gloss_range: to disbelieve, deny, cover over, or respond with ingratitude in the objectless post-table condition
words.root_gloss_range: covering, denial, disbelief, ingratitude, and unrelated lexical branches such as covering objects; the local Form I verb selects moral rejection after the sign
words.prose: {{ar:يَكْفُرْ}} ({{tr:yakfur}}) is jussive under the conditional particle, so the rejection is a possible future act after the table, not a past report. Because the verb has no explicit object, the table context keeps denial of the sign, covering over what has been shown, and ingratitude for provision together. Its basic Form I keeps the act direct rather than derived or intensified. The word is also the hinge of the ayah: it stands after descent and before punishment, echoing the covenant-warning pattern of 5:12 while shifting that earlier perfect breach into a future conditional possibility.

topics.headline: open jussive rejection
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the condition leaves the object of rejection unspoken, widening the warning within the table scene.
topics.reason: The verb is jussive after the conditional particle and has no explicit direct object in the local syntax.

topics.headline: covering and ingratitude after descent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels disbelief here as covering over a manifested gift and sign, while the local sense remains moral rejection rather than a farmer or night image becoming literal.
topics.reason: The root image supports covering and ingratitude, but the local Form I verb in the conditional warning selects disbelief or rejection after the table.

topics.headline: Form I future possibility
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees a direct basic act of rejection, clipped by the conditional mood and not intensified through a derived form.
topics.reason: The verb is Form I and jussive, contrasting with perfect forms in supplied parallels.

topics.headline: rejection links grant to punishment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the word as the condition that converts descent into the punishment consequence.
topics.reason: The verb stands in the protasis between the sending-down clause and the punishment apodosis.

topics.headline: 5:12 warning pattern reworked
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the near formula from 5:12, now applied to the table episode with a tense shift.
topics.reason: The rows provide the concrete 5:12 parallel and the local imperfect form marks a shifted conditional frame.

words.gloss_range: afterward, a compressed temporal adverb whose omitted complement is recovered from the table descent
words.root_gloss_range: temporal and spatial remoteness or after-position; locally temporal posteriority is selected, with threshold-distance pressure retained
words.prose: {{ar:بَعْدُ}} ({{tr:baʿdu}}) makes the condition specifically post-gift. Its cut construct form leaves the complement unspoken because the table event is already active; the word means afterward without having to repeat after what. The root's distance pressure turns that afterward into a threshold: if rejection happens after the descent, it comes from the far side of a decisive sign. The clipped form also recalls the fuller 5:12 covenant formula while sounding more compressed.

topics.headline: compressed post-table timing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the warning applies after the table event, with the time-reference compressed rather than vague.
topics.reason: The adverb is cut from its construct complement and functions as temporal modifier of the condition.

topics.headline: afterness as threshold distance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the temporal after as crossing a decisive threshold, while local grammar keeps the word temporal rather than spatial.
topics.reason: The root supports remoteness, but the local form is an adverb of time in the protasis.

topics.headline: 5:12 afterness compressed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the covenant-warning echo from 5:12, but in a shorter, sharper form.
topics.reason: The source rows explicitly compare the clipped local form with the fuller phrase in 5:12.

topics.headline: act-time-source sequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the protasis narrowing from rejection to post-sign timing before the source group is named.
topics.reason: The word sits between the conditional verb and the partitive group phrase.

words.gloss_range: from among you, partitive source within the addressed recipients
words.prose: {{ar:مِنكُمْ}} ({{tr:minkum}}) closes the protasis by locating the possible rejecter inside the addressed group. The preposition is partitive here: the warning does not name all recipients as rejecters, but it says any culprit would be drawn from among the very people who received the gift upon them. This small-domain source later contrasts with the final all-worlds domain.

topics.headline: possible rejecter from recipients
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that accountability is internal to the blessed group without making the whole group guilty.
topics.reason: The local grammar selects partitive extraction from the second-person plural addressees.

topics.headline: small domain anticipates universal domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah's scale begin with a subset of the recipients before expanding to no one among all worlds.
topics.reason: The same preposition appears later with the universal final domain, creating a local-to-cosmic contrast.

words.gloss_range: apodosis connector that binds the punishment clause to the condition
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) introduces the answer to the condition. It keeps the punishment clause from floating as a new assertion and makes it the consequence of whoever disbelieves afterward. As the second connector, it completes the visible chain begun by the first {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}): promise to condition, condition to consequence.

topics.headline: condition answered by consequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the punishment clause as syntactically bound to the condition, not as an independent threat.
topics.reason: The connector opens the apodosis of the conditional protasis.

topics.headline: second link in the connector chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader watches the ayah's cause-effect logic become visible through two matching connectors.
topics.reason: The first connector opens the condition, and this second connector opens the consequence with emphatic first-person speech.

words.gloss_range: emphatic first-person opening of the punishment consequence
words.prose: {{ar:إِنِّي}} ({{tr:innī}}) makes the consequence solemnly asserted. With the preceding connector it fuses consequence, emphasis, and first-person divine agency before the punishment verb arrives. It also mirrors the first emphatic opening, so the ayah balances the gift and the punishment in the same emphatic speech frame.

topics.headline: solemn consequence clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the punishment as a solemnly asserted divine consequence, not a bare result clause.
topics.reason: The emphatic particle with first-person suffix opens the apodosis predicate.

topics.headline: gift and punishment share a frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees promise and punishment as parallel divine commitments with opposite content.
topics.reason: The word repeats the earlier emphatic first-person frame and adds the apodosis connector.

words.gloss_range: I punish him, a direct first-person Form II punishment verb targeting whoever disbelieves
words.root_gloss_range: punishment, torment, punitive subjection, deprivation, and a separate sweetness/fresh-water pole; locally Form II selects punishing while polarity can color the table reversal
words.prose: {{ar:أُعَذِّبُهُ}} ({{tr:uʿadhdhibuhū}}) supplies the consequence itself. The first-person imperfect keeps divine agency explicit, while the suffix routes the punishment back to whoever disbelieves. Form II adds intensive causative force, and in this table context the root's opposite pole of sweetness or provision sharpens the reversal: rejected gift becomes suffering and deprivation. This first punishment verb also starts the threefold root chain that continues through the noun and the repeated verb.

topics.headline: direct first-person consequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the conditional subject become the specific object of a direct divine act.
topics.reason: The verb is first-person singular and the attached suffix is the direct object referring back to the conditional subject.

topics.headline: intensive causative punishment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the consequence as an active intensive punishment, not an impersonal or weakened outcome.
topics.reason: The local form is active Form II with doubled middle radical.

topics.headline: provision reversed into deprivation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses the table-gift setting sharpen the punishment as reversal of desired provision, while the local verb still means punish.
topics.reason: The root has a polarity field, but the Form II local verb selects punitive subjection; the provision context makes the reversal meaningful.

topics.headline: condition answered by punishment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks this verb as the structural answer to the act of rejection.
topics.reason: The verb is the main predicate of the apodosis answering the conditional protasis.

topics.headline: first beat of punishment echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears severity accumulate as the punishment root moves from verb to noun to repeated verb.
topics.reason: The same root appears in three consecutive consequence elements.

words.gloss_range: a punishment, an indefinite cognate accusative that intensifies and becomes qualified as unmatched
words.root_gloss_range: punishment, torment, experiential suffering, deprivation, and a separate freshness/sweetness pole; locally the noun selects punishment while the table context heightens reversal
words.prose: {{ar:عَذَابًا}} ({{tr:ʿadhāban}}) turns the punishment verb into an intensified measure: I punish him with a punishment. Its indefiniteness leaves the punishment open until the following negated clause defines it as without precedent, and in the table context it makes rejected provision turn into torment. Standing between the two punishment verbs, it is the hinge of the final subframe: verb, cognate noun, negated comparison. Its shared cadence with the later no-one term also ties the punishment to the universal no-one comparison.

topics.headline: punishment intensified by cognate noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the noun not as a new object but as an intensifier of the act already named.
topics.reason: The noun functions as cognate accusative after the matching punishment verb.

topics.headline: indefinite noun awaits qualifier
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the punishment magnified first, then defined by the following no-precedent clause.
topics.reason: The noun is indefinite accusative and is modified by the following negated qualifying clause.

topics.headline: freshness pole inverted into torment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses a rejected table-provision becoming torment, while the local noun remains punishment rather than sweetness.
topics.reason: The root's polarity is relevant in the provision context, but the local noun selects the punishment branch.

topics.headline: middle beat of final punishment frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears and sees the noun as the middle beat that turns direct threat into an unmatched-punishment comparison.
topics.reason: The noun is positioned between two same-root verbs and before the negated qualifier.

words.gloss_range: negation introducing the qualifying comparison clause
words.prose: {{ar:لَّا}} ({{tr:lā}}) pivots from intensification to unmatched comparison. After the cognate noun has made the punishment heavy, this negation opens the clause that defines it: no comparable punishment is assigned to anyone among the worlds. The particle therefore makes the final claim not just severe, but without precedent.

topics.headline: no comparable punishment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the sentence move from punishing to denying any comparable punished case.
topics.reason: The negation scopes over the second punishment verb and the following universal object phrase.

topics.headline: punishment defined by negated qualifier
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the punishment's identity supplied by the clause that says what has no precedent.
topics.reason: The clause beginning here modifies the preceding indefinite punishment noun.

words.gloss_range: I punish with it or punish him, repeated under negation inside the qualifying comparison clause
words.root_gloss_range: punishment, torment, and punitive subjection; locally the same Form II punishment verb reappears under negation to define unmatched comparison
words.prose: {{ar:أُعَذِّبُهُ}} ({{tr:uʿadhdhibuhū}}) returns under negation, so the same intensive verb shifts function: first it threatened the rejecter, now it measures whether such punishment has ever applied to anyone else. The imperfect under negation supports a general no-precedent force, and the repeated form keeps the comparison tied to the specific punishment just named. As the third punishment-root beat, it completes the verb-noun-verb severity chain. From here the clause drives toward the no-one-among-worlds phrase, expanding the measure to cosmic scope.

topics.headline: general no-precedent verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the negated verb as a general comparison claim, not only a closed past-tense report.
topics.reason: The verb is imperfect under negation in the clause qualifying the punishment noun.

topics.headline: same intensive form becomes measure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the comparison uses the exact punishment form already threatened, so no lighter standard replaces it.
topics.reason: The second verb repeats the same Form II surface and its suffix sustains reference to the punishment measure.

topics.headline: punishment compared against all beings
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the verb propel the clause into a no-one comparison across the worlds.
topics.reason: The verb takes the following universal object phrase in the negated qualifier.

topics.headline: third punishment-root beat
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the final return of the punishment root complete the three-beat severity chain.
topics.reason: The identical verb returns after the cognate noun and under negation.

words.gloss_range: anyone, not a single one, as an indefinite singular object under negation
words.root_gloss_range: one, single, anyone, uniqueness, and indivisible singularity; locally the indefinite accusative under negation selects no-one scope, not the definite divine-name register
words.prose: {{ar:أَحَدًا}} ({{tr:aḥadan}}) makes the negation exhaustive by denying even one comparand. Its singular indefinite form under negation means no one whatsoever, and it tests the claim person by person before the domain expands to all worlds. Its -an cadence also pairs the no-one term with the punishment noun. The word also makes the same-surah reversal sharp: 5:20 uses the no-one-among-the-worlds field for unprecedented gift, while 5:115 uses it for unprecedented punishment.

topics.headline: not a single one
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the claim denies the smallest possible precedent before it expands to the worlds.
topics.reason: The word is indefinite singular accusative inside the negative clause.

topics.headline: comparand supplied to negated verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees exactly where the no-precedent comparison becomes grammatically explicit.
topics.reason: The word is the object of the negated punishment verb.

topics.headline: uniqueness routed into no-one scope
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels singularity strengthen the denial, while the indefinite form blocks reading it as the definite divine name.
topics.reason: The root can support uniqueness, but the local indefinite accusative under negation selects anyone or not a single one.

topics.headline: 5:20 formula inverted
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes a same-surah scope formula turned from unprecedented gift in 5:20 into unmatched punishment in 5:115.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows provide the concrete 5:20 echo and its inversion in the local punishment clause.

topics.headline: universal tail and cadence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the local warning expand into a universal closing tail and hears the accusative cadence tie punishment to anyone.
topics.reason: The word begins the final universal object phrase and shares cadence with the punishment noun.

words.gloss_range: from among or belonging to, opening the final universal domain phrase
words.prose: {{ar:مِنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) opens the final domain that completes the no-one comparison. It governs the worlds phrase and turns the preceding no-one term into a universal search set: not one from among the worlds. It also answers the earlier from-among-you phrase, expanding the scale from a possible member from among you to no one from among all worlds.

topics.headline: final world-domain preposition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the preposition launch the domain against which the punishment has no precedent.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the final worlds phrase and specifies the domain of the negated object.

topics.headline: from among you to from among worlds
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the repeated preposition zoom from local accountability to universal comparison.
topics.reason: The ayah uses the preposition first with the addressed group and finally with the worlds domain.

words.gloss_range: the worlds, all realms or communities of beings as the final comparison domain
words.root_gloss_range: worlds, realms, communities of beings, knowable domains, knowledge/sign associations; locally the definite plural selects total created-domain scope
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ}} ({{tr:al-ʿālamīna}}) is the ayah's final landing point. As a definite plural after the preposition, it completes the phrase no one from the worlds and gives the punishment comparison its maximum domain. The sound masculine plural can treat the worlds as populated communities of accountable beings, while the word's knowledge and sign associations remain secondary color: locally it is the total comparison set. The closing also reverses the worlds-frame of 5:20, where unmatched gift becomes, here, unmatched punishment.

topics.headline: definite plural total domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the final word set the widest comparison field for the unmatched punishment.
topics.reason: The word is definite genitive plural after the preposition, completing the universal domain phrase.

topics.headline: sound plural treats worlds as communities
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the domain distributed across populated realms rather than flattened into one mass.
topics.reason: The sound masculine plural form supports the community-like treatment noted in the source grammar.

topics.headline: knowable sign-filled domains
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses the final domain as knowable and sign-filled, while the local syntax keeps the selected sense as worlds or realms.
topics.reason: The root field supports knowledge and sign associations, but the local noun in this phrase means worlds as a domain.

topics.headline: punishment measured cosmically
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the punishment's severity measured against the whole created order, not only the addressed group.
topics.reason: The word closes the negated comparison clause and is linked to the punishment root field.

topics.headline: worlds-frame gift reversed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the worlds-scope of 5:20 turned from unparalleled giving into unparalleled punishment at the ayah's close.
topics.reason: The rows give a concrete same-surah echo and a closing frame from named divine speech to all worlds.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The caused descent, followed by fa-man, ba'du, kufr, and the repeated punishment root.
baseline_models.mechanism: The divine utterance commits the object to delivery; its arrival creates a temporal threshold, and denial after that threshold activates the stated sanction.

activation_trace.role: Caused descent and delivery supply the event that changes the recipients' evidentiary position.
Denial and obstruction of acknowledged truth supply the offense after delivery.
Succession after a prior event makes the descent a liability boundary.
Painful punishment, repeated as verb-noun-verb, supplies the consequence and gives it emphatic density.

changed_reading.before: A promise of descent followed by a general warning against unbelief.
changed_reading.after: Delivery creates a post-event liability threshold: the punished condition is denial after receipt, not uncertainty before receipt.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Munazziluha, yakfur, and the ensuing punishment.
baseline_models.mechanism: The descent root can present the object as provision prepared for a guest, while kufr can cover a blessing; the warning can therefore concern betrayal of received hospitality as well as propositional denial.

activation_trace.role: Provision prepared for a guest makes the descended object readable as hosted gift.
Covering a blessing turns post-receipt kufr into ingratitude toward the giver.
Punitive pain becomes the response to a gift received and then denied.

changed_reading.before: The object is unspecified and kufr is only doctrinal disbelief.
changed_reading.after: The object can already be heard as guest-provision, making kufr a breach of gratitude and hospitality.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The triple use of the punishment root in 'a punishment with which I punish no one among the worlds.'
baseline_models.mechanism: Negated ahad exhausts the comparison class, while the marker branch of the worlds-root makes the sanction not merely intense but distinguishing across the widest named field.

activation_trace.role: Repeated punishment supplies the event being compared across all others.
Ahad under negation exhausts every possible comparator rather than naming one individual.
A distinguishing mark supplies an exploratory way to hear the worlds as the field across which this case is singularly marked.

changed_reading.after: The punishment is also a singular identifying mark, with no comparator anywhere in the stated world-field.

context_deltas.mechanism: Earlier consumable provision is repeatedly governed as a test, and 5:94 supplies the same whoever-offends-afterward-punishment frame. The focus ayah escalates from reachable game and transgression to a requested descended provision and kufr, and from painful punishment to an unmatched one.

activation_trace.role: An edible share or provision begins the pericope's treatment of food as a governed gift.
An apportioned gift identifies consumable goods as received provision rather than autonomous possession.
A test that reveals condition makes accessible food-material an evidentiary trial.
Afterward succession supplies the earlier legal threshold echoed by the focus.
Punitive pain completes the earlier offense-after-threshold consequence.
Actual delivery raises the focus test from reachable provision to a sign brought upon the recipients.
Denial of truth intensifies the earlier transgression into an evidentiary rupture.

structural_cues: 5:87-96 repeatedly joins food or game, divine provision, protective conduct, breach, and consequence.
5:94 and 5:115 share a whoever-offends-afterward-punishment sequence, while 5:115 intensifies both offense and sanction.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the recurring provision-test sequence and the close conditional syntax; I infer a deliberate escalation in evidentiary access and liability. A live alternative is that 5:94 contributes only a common warning formula.

changed_reading.after: The climax of progressive provision-tests: greater access to a requested gift produces a sharper post-receipt liability.

context_deltas.mechanism: Earlier food-law breaches receive kaffara, a covering of fault enacted through feeding; the focus instead uses yakfur for covering the descended sign itself. Food shifts from the means of reparative covering to the object around which culpable covering occurs.

activation_trace.role: Expiatory covering supplies a reparative use of the same root later used for disbelief.
Feeding others is the material operation by which the earlier breach is covered.
A second food-law expiation reinforces compensatory covering as an established repair pattern.
Food for the needy again materializes repair through feeding.
The focus reverses covering from removal of fault to concealment or denial of manifest truth.
Guest-provision makes the reparative-versus-culpable covering contrast specifically food-shaped.

structural_cues: Both 5:89 and 5:95 specify food-based compensatory schedules for bounded breaches.
The focus retains the food setting and the k-f-r root but stipulates a conditional sanction rather than a compensatory schedule.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the shared root and repeated feeding remedies; I infer an intentional semantic reversal between covering fault and covering a sign. The alternative is that kaffara and kufr should remain separate conventional senses with no local wordplay.

changed_reading.before: Kufr is a generic label for disbelief after a miracle.
changed_reading.after: Kufr becomes an anti-expiatory reversal: where food previously covered a breach, the recipient now covers the divine food-sign.

context_deltas.mechanism: The packet first warns that requested disclosure can trouble its requesters, then recalls people who asked for a feminine object and became disbelievers in it. The table request and the focus promise of descending it instantiate that warned sequence.

activation_trace.role: Questioning and requesting initiate a disclosure for which the requester becomes responsible.
The emergence of what was hidden supplies the transition from uncertainty to exposed evidence.
Ongoing delivery links asking to disclosure during something sent down.
A prior community's request supplies the explicit precedent for self-requested evidence.
Their subsequent disbelief supplies the exact failure anticipated in the focus.
Afterward closes the request-disclosure cycle before liability begins.

structural_cues: 5:102 uses a feminine singular object in both asking for it and becoming disbelievers in it; 5:112-115 repeats a feminine table and the promise to descend it.
The sequence runs warning about requests, precedent of post-request kufr, present request, promised disclosure, then post-disclosure kufr.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated request-disclosure-kufr sequence and feminine pronouns; I infer that the earlier warning frames the table episode without asserting an identical antecedent. The alternative is a broad thematic recurrence rather than a precise foreshadowing.

changed_reading.before: Ba'du merely means later than the descent.
changed_reading.after: Ba'du marks completion of a warned, voluntarily initiated request-disclosure cycle, so the liability is partly self-incurred.

context_deltas.mechanism: The pronoun is resolved as a food-laden table requested from above and named as provision and a sign. Its requesters state the outcomes they seek: eating, settled hearts, verified truthfulness, and witness. Descent therefore fulfills both divine hospitality and a self-declared evidentiary contract.

activation_trace.role: Requested descent activates the guest-provision branch and makes the table a hosted meal.
A tray or table bearing food resolves the focus pronoun to a communal edible object.
Actual eating makes bodily receipt one declared purpose of the sign.
Settling into reassurance supplies the affective result the requesters say the sign should produce.
Fulfillment of word by deed supplies the truth claim the table is asked to verify.
Presence with direct observation makes the recipients prospective witnesses, not remote hearers.
A manifest sign makes the table's evidentiary function explicit.
Apportioned giving names the meal as divine provision and reinforces the host-gift mechanism.
Covering a blessing becomes the breach after every requested mode of assurance has been supplied.

structural_cues: The request says 'upon us' in 5:112 and 5:114; the answer shifts to 'upon you' in 5:115, transferring the requested object into recipient responsibility.
The declared chain is bodily receipt, affective settlement, knowledge of fulfilled truth, and public witness before the warning says 'afterward.'
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the table, provision, sign, and the requesters' stated aims; I treat those aims as a self-set burden of proof that fulfillment discharges. A live alternative is that they are motives rather than a binding evidentiary contract.

changed_reading.before: Disbelief follows an externally imposed miracle.
changed_reading.after: Disbelief would repudiate a hosted sign the recipients requested and whose evidentiary success criteria they specified themselves.

context_deltas.mechanism: Immediately before the table dialogue, manifest proofs are met by kufr through relabeling them as evident magic. Since the table is explicitly called a sign, post-descent kufr can operate as interpretive recoding of acknowledged visibility rather than simple denial that an event occurred.

activation_trace.role: Manifest appearance supplies proofs whose visibility is conceded even while their meaning is contested.
Denial of truth supplies the response to already manifest proofs.
Magic as diversion and deception supplies the rival label used to neutralize a sign.
The table's designation as a manifest sign makes the earlier recoding pattern available to the focus.
Focus kufr can therefore be active obstruction of a sign's disclosed meaning.

structural_cues: 5:110 places manifest proofs, kufr, and the counter-label 'magic' in one response sequence.
5:114 designates the requested table as a sign before 5:115 warns against kufr after its descent.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an earlier mechanism for resisting visible proofs; I infer that it exemplifies how post-table kufr could work. The alternative is that the table's rejection would take a different form not specified here.

changed_reading.before: Kufr means refusing to believe that the descended event happened.
changed_reading.after: Kufr may concede the event yet cover its force by redescribing the manifest sign as deception.

context_deltas.mechanism: The table exchange stands inside a sequence opened by the day God gathers the messengers and closed by another divine saying about the day truthfulness benefits the truthful. The focus utterance can function both as the original promise and as archived testimony replayed in final accounting.

activation_trace.role: A bounded span identified as the gathering day supplies the judicial temporal frame.
Gathering dispersed messengers supplies the assembly in which testimony is reviewed.
Spoken question and answer initiate the judgment dialogue that leads into the recalled exchange.
A second divine saying closes the extended speech sequence as a judgment pronouncement.

Benefit opposed to harm supplies the favorable judgment counterpart to the focus punishment.
The focus saying becomes an evidentiary utterance preserved within the larger divine-human dialogue.

structural_cues: 5:109 opens with the day of gathering and interrogated responses; 5:110 and 5:116 each begin a divine address to Jesus around the table exchange.
5:115 and 5:119 both begin with 'God said,' and 5:119 explicitly returns to 'this day' and truthfulness.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the judgment opening, repeated divine speech frames, and the truthfulness close; I infer that the table promise is replayable evidence inside final accounting. The alternative is a historical flashback merely juxtaposed with, rather than embedded in, the judgment scene.

context_deltas.mechanism: The nearby final dialogue places punishment and forgiveness as alternatives concerning God's servants, and the close reserves dominion to God. This weakens any expansion of the focus threat into a humanly administered or indiscriminate verdict, without erasing its explicit condition.

activation_trace.role: Punitive pain is restated as an if-clause under divine action rather than human assignment.
Servitude and ownership keep the persons under God's claim even in the punishment branch.
Covering sin and shielding its bearer preserves forgiveness as language in the final adjudicative scene.
Sovereign dominion reserves classification and execution of judgment to God.
The focus retains a severe first-person sanction, but only under its stated post-descent kufr condition.

structural_cues: 5:115 says 'whoever disbelieves afterward,' restricting the sanction to a predicate rather than every recipient.
5:118 pairs 'if You punish' with 'if You forgive,' and 5:120 closes with God's exclusive dominion.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies conditional threat, conditional punishment-forgiveness language, and sovereign ownership; I infer a scope check against reader-made universalization. A live alternative is that 5:118 concerns a different category and does not soften the certainty of 5:115 for anyone who meets its predicate.

changed_reading.before: An automatic and humanly classifiable doom for all who encounter the table.
changed_reading.after: A severe divine conditional sentence whose predicate must not be broadened beyond actual post-sign kufr and whose adjudication remains God's.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the same focus root field contains palatable sweetness and punitive pain. It remains anchored in the triple focus occurrence and the descended food setting, but downstream prose should present it only as a lexical counterpoint, not claim that punishment is sweet or that one sense historically derives from the other.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The three ع ذ ب occurrences immediately after the descent of the food-sign.

activation_trace.role: Palatable sweetness in water or food supplies the positive sensory pole made available by the root field.
Punitive pain supplies the overt focus sense and violently reverses the sweetness pole.
Eating makes palatability materially relevant rather than an unrelated dictionary association.
Nourishing sustenance sharpens the inversion from received food to inflicted pain.

changed_reading.before: The food-sign and the punishment are adjacent but semantically separate.
changed_reading.after: The root field produces a contained sensory reversal: palatable provision flips into the most emphatic punitive pain when the gift is covered.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is branch-distant because the surface table need not mean oscillation. It remains useful as a packet-anchored counterpoint among the table's m-y-d motion field, the request for settled hearts, and the focus branch of putting something in its station; downstream prose should qualify it as word-field play, not define the table as unstable.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Munazziluha as placing the object into its station, followed by kufr as renewed covering.

activation_trace.role: Motion, disturbance, and inclination supply an exploratory unstable pole within the table's root field.
Stillness and reassurance supply the explicitly desired stabilization of the recipients.
Putting a thing in its proper station supplies the focus act that resolves movement into placement.
Covering again supplies the reversal by which disclosed and stabilized evidence is obscured.

changed_reading.before: The table descends simply to provide proof.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, a motion-laden table is placed to settle wavering hearts, so later kufr is a renewed destabilizing cover after placement and reassurance.

strongest_changes: The exact 5:94 offense-afterward-punishment frame turns 5:115 into an escalated culmination of provision-tests.
The 5:101-102 request-disclosure-kufr warning is instantiated by the requested feminine table and the promise to descend it.
The requesters specify eating, settled hearts, verified truth, and witness, making post-descent kufr a repudiation of their own evidence contract.
Food-based kaffara earlier in the pericope reverses into yakfur against the food-sign, while the judgment frame preserves the promise as evidence.
summary.what_was_special: A requested food-sign converges with hospitality, expiation, testing, disclosure, witness, and final judgment in one small word, ba'du: after receipt, the recipient's epistemic and covenantal position has changed.
remaining_uncertainties: Whether ba'du presupposes eating from the table or only its descent.
Whether 5:109-119 embeds the whole table exchange in the judgment scene or juxtaposes a historical flashback with it.
How much weight the sweetness-punishment and movement-settlement branch counterpoints can bear beyond contained lexical play.
Whether the forgiveness language of 5:118 addresses the same predicate as 5:115 or a broader, categorically different population.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Granted visibility intensifies later concealment.** `ن ز ل B002` is sending down, `ك ف ر B001` concealment, `ب ع د B002` afterness, and `ع ذ ب B005` punishment. The sequence makes liability depend on rejection after the requested sign. I infer that customized disclosure narrows future ambiguity and therefore magnifies repudiation.
2. **Uniqueness of consequence mirrors uniqueness of request.** `ء ح د B005` can distribute individual-by-individual. I infer that the unparalleled punishment answers a collectively requested but personally borne evidentiary burden.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later ayah 5:120 made the fixed ayah's local distinctions newly visible as bounded operations within a single encompassing dominion, rather than as an isolated rule or episode.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Granted descent converts requested proof into exceptional liability.** Fixed **ن ز ل / B002** (“bringing down or sending down”) and **B010** (“one descent or episode”) make the promised table a bounded historical delivery. 5:112–5:114 supplied the demand, intended calm, witness, sign, and communal return; 5:116 begins the final audit of what people later attributed to Jesus. I infer that denial after a self-requested, fulfilled sign violates a denser chain of acknowledged evidence than denial before it. The severe warning reads as consequence of proof entering communal custody.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 5:116 showed the post-sign danger anticipated here: granted proof can later be misattributed, so custody includes preserving the giver-agent distinction.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه قال يقول قولا، والقول والقيل، والكلام المركب من الحروف إذا أبرز بالنطق، مفردا كان أو جملة أو قصيدة أو خطبة.
branches.source_phrase_ar: القول من النطق (maqayis)؛ قال يقول قولا وقولة ومقالا ومقالة (sihah)؛ القول والقيل واحد (mufradat)؛ المركب من الحروف المبرز بالنطق (mufradat)؛ القيل من القول اسم (ayn)

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه المقول بمعنى اللسان.
يدخل فيه قولة وقوال وقوالة وتقوالة وقؤول ومقوال ومقول إذا وصفت الإنسان بأنه لسن أو كثير القول أو منطيق.
يدخل فيه المقول أو القيل بلغة أهل اليمن، والواحد القيل، والجمع المقاولة والأقيال والأقوال، وملك حمير دون الملك الأعظم، والمرأة قيلة.

branches.branch_image_ar: قول ما لم يكن أو نسبته
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه تقول باطلا، وتقول عليه أي كذب عليه، وقولتني أو أقولتني ما لم أقل.
يدخل فيه اقتال قولا إذا اجتر إلى نفسه قولا من خير أو شر.
يدخل فيه القالة الحسنة أو القبيحة المنتشرة في الناس، وكثرة قالة الناس، والقيل والقال بوصفهما حديثا دائرا.
يدخل فيه القال، الخشبة التي تضرب بها القلة.
يدخل فيه قاولته في أمره وتقاولنا إذا تفاوضنا.
يدخل فيه اقتال عليه إذا كان بمعنى تحكم.
يدخل فيه تقول إذا أجري مجرى تظن في العمل، وخاصة في الاستفهام، وما ذكر عن بني سليم من إجراء متصرف قلت مجرى الظن في غير الاستفهام.
يدخل فيه المتصور في النفس قبل الإبراز باللفظ، كما في قول في نفسي لم أظهره.
يدخل فيه القول بمعنى الاعتقاد، نحو فلان يقول بقول أبي حنيفة.
يدخل فيه القول للدلالة على الشيء، مثل امتلأ الحوض وقال قطني.
يدخل فيه فلان يقول بكذا إذا كان معناه العناية الصادقة بالشيء.
يدخل فيه استعمال المنطقيين القول بمعنى الحد، كقول الجوهر وقول العرض أي حدهما.
يدخل فيه القول في الإلهام، حيث يسمى إلقاء المعنى قولا من غير خطاب وارد.

branches.what_is_ar: القليل والقِلَّة ضد الكثرة، ويدخل فيه الافتقار والذلة، وتقليل الشيء في العين، واستقلاله، واستعمال القليل للنفي أو للندرة
قُلَّة الجبل وأعلى كل شيء، ورأس الإنسان، وقبيعة السيف
القُلَّة إناء كالجرة الكبيرة، ومنها قلال هجر والحباب العظام
حمل الشيء واحتماله، وارتفاعه أو نهوضه، وارتحال القوم ظاعنين
القِلُّ رعدة أو انتفاض يأخذ الإنسان من فزع أو غضب
القلقلة والتقلقل: صوت الحركة، وتحريك الشيء حتى يتحرك ويضطرب، وقلة الثبوت في المكان

root_profile.summary: Kök, azlık; bir şeyin tepesi veya başı; büyük bir kap; yük taşıma, yükselme ve yola koyulma; korku ya da öfkeden titreme; nesnenin oynayıp yerinde duramaması ve hareket sesi olmak üzere altı ayrı anlam kolunda düzenlenir.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه أله وتأله بمعنى عبد وتنسك، والتأليه بمعنى التعبيد، والإله والآلهة والإلاهة لما جعل معبودا.
يدخل فيه اسم الله والقول في أصله من إله، وصيغ الاستعمال مثل الله ما فعلت بمعنى والله، واللهم، ويا الله، ولاه أبوك أو لاه أنت ونحوها.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi günahı veya bozulan yeminin doğurduğu yükü belirli bir karşılıkla örtme, silme ve işlenmemiş gibi kılma sürecini açıkça destekler.

lexicalization_scope.note: Günah yükünü giderme çekirdeği korunur; bozulmuş yemin için gerekeni yapma yalnızca ilgili söz öbeğine bağlı özel gerçekleşmedir.

concept_map.definition: Bir günahın ya da bozulan yeminin doğurduğu yükü, gereken karşılığı veya işlemi yerine getirerek örtmek, silmek ve işlenmemiş sayılacak duruma getirmektir.

facets.statement: Günahın yükünü örten veya silen karşılık ya da işlem.
Bozulan yemin için gereken yükümlülüğü yerine getirme, çekirdeğin yapıya bağlı özel türüdür.
İşlemin sonucu, kötülüğün işlenmemiş gibi değerlendirilmesi veya etkisinin silinmesidir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar günahın veya yeminin yükünü gideren karşılıkta birleşir; toplu anlatım hem gereken eylemi hem de günahın silinmiş sayılması sonucunu korur.

concept_gloss.applicability: Hem giderici işlemi hem de günahın etkisinin silinmesi sonucunu kapsayan genel karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Günah yükünün bir karşılık veya işlemle ortadan kaldırılmasını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Yemin bozulduğunda doğan özel yükümlülüğün yerine getirildiği bağlamda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Bozulan yemin nedeniyle gereken karşılığın yerine getirilmesini korur.
error_profile.loses: Yemin dışındaki günah ve kötülüklerin giderilmesini dışarıda bırakır.

contextual_glosses.applicability: İşlemin günahı işlenmemiş gibi kılan sonucunun öne çıktığı bağlamda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Günahın etkisini ve yükünü ortadan kaldırma sonucunu korur.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه باعد وأبعد وبعده تبعيدا والمباعدة، أي جعل الشيء بعيدا أو فصل بين شيئين أو أمعن في الذهاب
يدخل فيه بعد بمعنى هلك، وبعدا له وسحقا، وأبعده الله في اللعن والدعاء بالإقصاء عن الخير
يدخل فيه الأباعد والأبعدون والبعدان ومن بعدان الأمير، أي من بعدت منزلته أو قرابته أو صلته في مقابل الأقارب والقربان
يدخل فيه الصيغ المحفوظة مثل تنح غير باعد أي غير صاغر، وتنح غير بعيد أي كن قريبا، وهم مني غير بعد أي ليسوا ببعيد
يدخل فيه لقيته بعيدات بين ونحوه، أي يقع اللقاء أو الفعل بعد حين ثم ينقطع ثم يعود
يدخل فيه ذو بعدة وذو بعد رأي، أي نافذ الرأي ذو غور وحزم
يدخل فيه غير أبعد وما عندك أبعد وبغير أبعد، أي لا خير فيه أو لا طائل ولا منفعة

identity_judgment.rationale: Yetkili ifade, suyun tatlı, hoş ve tuzlu olmayan niteliğini merkeze alırken kolay tüketilen başka yiyecek ve içecekleri de kapsar. Tatlı su arama, suyu tatlı bulma ve iki belirli sıvıyı birlikte adlandırma kullanımları bu niteliğe bağlı yan kullanımlardır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım hem yalın nitelik bildiren biçimleri hem de tatlı su edinme, arama veya öyle sayma yapılarıyla sınırlı kullanımları ayrı tutar.

concept_map.definition: Su başta olmak üzere bir yiyecek veya içeceğin tatlı, hoş ve kolay tüketilir olması; su için ayrıca tuzlu olmama niteliğini taşır. Bu niteliğe bağlı yapılar tatlı su edinmeyi, aramayı ya da bir şeyi tatlı saymayı anlatabilir.

facets.statement: Bir yiyecek veya içeceğin damakta hoş, tatlı ve kolay tüketilir olmasıdır.
Su söz konusu olduğunda hoş içimin yanında tuzlu olmama niteliği belirgindir.
Belirli yapılarda tatlı su edinme veya arama ve bir şeyi tatlı sayma anlatılır.
Bir ikili adlandırma tükürük ile şarabı birlikte bu hoşluk niteliği altında anar.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak çekirdeği tatlı, hoş ve kolay tüketilen su, yiyecek veya içecektir; su edinme, arama ve tatlı sayma kullanımları bu çekirdeğe bağlanır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Yetkili ifade ağır acı verme ve cezalandırma çekirdeğini doğrular. Bunun dayaktan türediği ve sonra her ağır sıkıntıya aktarıldığı açıklaması ortak zorunlu anlam değil, bildirilen bir köken ve genişleme görüşüdür; dal ancak bu kayıtla kabul edilebilir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım ad, eylem ve yok etmeye yönelik ceza yapısını ayırır; yapıya bağlı özel ceza bütün dala genellenmez.

concept_map.definition: Birine ağır acı çektirme veya onu ağır biçimde cezalandırmadır. Dayak kökeni ve anlamın her türlü ağır sıkıntıya yayılması, çekirdeğin parçası değil aktarılan bir açıklamadır.

facets.statement: Bir kişiye ağır acı verilir veya ağır bir ceza uygulanır.
Belirli bir yapı, bütünüyle yok etmeye yönelik cezayı anlatır.
Bildirilen bir görüş anlamı dayaktan başlatır ve sonra her ağır sıkıntıya genişletir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Ortak çekirdek ağır acı verme ve cezalandırmadır; dayak kökeni ile her ağır sıkıntıya yayılma ise zorunlu anlamdan ayrı, aktarılan bir açıklamadır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Hem uygulanan ağır cezayı hem de birine şiddetli acı verme eylemini karşılayan çekirdek ifadedir.

error_profile.preserves: Ağır acı verme ile ceza uygulama bileşenlerini birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Eyleyenin başka bir kişiye şiddetli acı verdiği bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Eyleyeni, etkileneni ve ağır acının verilmesini korur.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه العذاب والعقوبة والإيجاع الشديد، والتعذيب، وما يذكره المصدر من أصل الضرب ثم استعارة كل شدة.
branches.source_phrase_ar: العذاب يقال منه عذب تعذيبا وناس يقولون أصل العذاب الضرب ثم استعير ذلك في كل شدة (maqayis)؛ عذبت الرجل وغيره تعذيبا والاسم العذاب (jamhara)؛ العذاب العقوبة وقد عذبته تعذيبا (sihah)؛ العذاب هو الإيجاع الشديد (mufradat)

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه طرف السوط واللسان، والخرقة أو السير المشدود، والخيط، والغصن، وأطراف السيور والشراك، وما كان من علاقة أو ذوابة متدلية.
يدخل فيه العذبة بمعنى القذاة في الماء، وكثرة القذى، وإزالة ما في الحوض من القذى أو عرمضه، مع شاهد تهذيب عن ماء لا رعي فيه ولا كلأ.
يدخل فيه وصف العذبي بمعنى الكريم الأخلاق.
يدخل فيه العذب الخارج على أثر الولد من الرحم، والعذابة بمعنى الرحم.
